title: Paragraph purpose
summary: Give every paragraph one controlling point or narrative function, select only details that perform that job and use paragraph boundaries to make the response easy to follow.

sections.title: Turn each plan job into one paragraph promise
content: E6.5 produced a route in which every body paragraph had a job. Before drafting, turn each job into a paragraph promise: a short statement of the single contribution that the paragraph must make to the composition's controlling focus.

For the charity-sale response, body paragraph one promises to show how dividing the event into tasks created a manageable initial plan. Body paragraph two promises to show how the same method supported adaptation after rain changed the venue. These jobs are connected but not interchangeable.

sections.title: Use purpose, evidence and meaning
content: Build an explanatory paragraph through three moves: purpose, evidence and meaning. The purpose states the paragraph's controlling point. The evidence supplies precise actions, observations or examples. The meaning explains how that evidence advances the composition's central response.

This is a control model, not a rigid three-sentence formula. A paragraph may need several evidence and explanation sentences, but they should all serve the same promise. A sentence that cannot be connected to the promise should be moved, reframed or removed.

sections.title: See one explanatory job performed
content: Purpose: dividing the sale into task areas made the original workload manageable. Evidence: the organisers separated publicity, supplies, prices and staffing, assigned a deadline to each area and used the list to notice that no one had confirmed the drinks order. Meaning: instead of reacting to one large, vague problem, the group could see and complete one responsibility at a time.

The missing drinks order belongs because it demonstrates the value of the task breakdown. The colour of a poster does not belong unless the writer can show how it affected the planning method. Relevance is decided by the paragraph promise, not merely by whether a detail happened at the event.

sections.title: Give narrative paragraphs a dominant function
content: In narrative writing, a paragraph's promise may be functional rather than argumentative: establish a situation, trigger a problem, intensify pressure, reveal a turning point, show a consequence or resolve the conflict. A paragraph can contain action, description and thought while still having one dominant function.

For the sale example, the rain paragraph's dominant function is disruption and adaptation. The first drops, the hurried move and the decision to prioritise electrical safety all belong to that stage. A long history of the school hall would interrupt rather than perform the function.

sections.title: Place boundaries where the job changes
content: Start a new paragraph when the controlling point or narrative function changes. A meaningful shift in time, place, speaker or stage may signal that change, but the shift matters because it gives the writing a new job—not because every new action needs a new paragraph.

Keep closely connected evidence and explanation together. Avoid one-sentence fragments that split a single job into pieces, and avoid block paragraphs that hide several unrelated jobs. Ask: ‘Would one short purpose label still describe every sentence here?’

sections.title: Reverse-outline the draft
content: After drafting, label each paragraph in three to seven words. ‘Create the initial task plan’ and ‘Adapt the method after rain’ reveal useful progression. Repeated labels expose repetition; a label containing ‘and also something else’ exposes mixed purposes; ‘miscellaneous details’ exposes a paragraph with no controlling job.

Repair repetition by combining paragraphs or giving the later one a new contribution. Repair a mixed paragraph by choosing its controlling point and moving the other material. Repair a purposeless paragraph by linking useful evidence to a job or deleting it.

sections.title: Control the paragraph route
content: Make six decisions about paragraph promises, supporting sentences, boundaries, narrative function and reverse-outline repair. Complete the group before viewing feedback.
